invariants: This movement reports; it does not repair.
Dependency verification and locking are never weakened to make a check pass.
No credential, management address, device name or serial enters a tracked file or a report.
No vendor data collection and no device contact: the standing collection gate holds.
No contract status is applied, removed or changed.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review of the diff plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not merge to main.
report.objective: Run the ui2/ Java acceptance checks on this machine for the first time and report exactly what passes, what fails and what cannot run, with the real command output. Fix nothing; the point is an honest baseline.
output_contract: A DRAFT report recording, per acceptance check, the command, the exit code, the counts and the first failure
SESSION_CLOSE with the real output of every check and an explicit statement of anything that could not be run and why

recommended_reasoning.reason: Running documented commands and writing down what happened. The only discipline required is not fixing what it finds.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law
Report what the commands did, never what they were expected to do. A check that fails is a finding, not a problem to be worked around.
Do not pass --offline, --refresh-dependencies, --write-locks, --update-locks or any flag that weakens dependency verification or locking. If a check cannot run without one, that is the finding.
If a run takes longer than the movement can afford, report how far it got rather than reporting a result it did not observe.
Quote failure output rather than summarising it away, but keep each excerpt bounded and never reproduce a credential, address or device identity from any log.
Publish SESSION_CLOSE with scripts/local_relay.py append using --report pointing at a JSON file you wrote first. Do not pass report JSON inline on the command line.
Do not merge to main. Commit on the lane and publish SESSION_CLOSE.
risks: Fixing a failure in passing, so the baseline reports a repaired state rather than the real one.
Weakening verification or locking to get check to pass.
Reporting a suite result that was never observed because the run was cut short.
Standing up a database to make integrationTest run, which belongs to the deployment movement and would change what is being measured.

in: Run each acceptance check B1-1a section 7 names that does not require a database, and record the real output of each: the module listing, architectureTest, unitTest, and check
Record for architectureTest whether all ten direction methods ran and passed, by name

Determine whether integrationTest can run here at all, and report the finding rather than forcing it: it requires a real PostgreSQL 16, and the contract states the command must fail rather than skip when none is available
Write one short report under docs/design/ recording, per check, the command, the exit code, the counts, and the first failure if any -- status DRAFT, no contract status applied
Where a check fails, record the failure and its likely locus precisely enough for a later movement to act, and stop there
out: Fixing anything the run reveals: this movement reports, it does not repair
Changing any Java source, build script, lockfile, verification metadata or test
Regenerating dependency locks or verification metadata, or passing any flag that weakens dependency verification
Installing or provisioning a database, or standing up any part of the deployment: the deployment movement owns that
Any change under ui2/frontend/, project/, relay/ or .github/workflows/
Applying, removing or changing any contract status
Any vendor data collection or device contact
